newsitem.title: CROATIA: Levi Strauss agrees to extend licence in Croatia.
newsitem.headline: Levi Strauss agrees to extend licence in Croatia.

text.p: Croatia's largest textile firm Varteks Denim on Thursday signed an agreement with U.S. clothing giant Levi Strauss & Co. on extending its manufacturing licence for another five years, Croatian radio said.
Varteks general manager Andjelko Herjavec and Varteks Denim's director Davor Darabos undertook a commitment to fully privatise the firm by the end of 1998, the radio said.
Levi Strauss earlier threatened to withdraw the licence because of the firm's unresolved ownership structure. Varteks Denim's current licence expires on June 30.
More than one half of the concern's basic capital -- some 300 million kuna (81 million marks) -- is still state-owned. The rest is owned by small shareholders.
Varteks also agreed to secure drainage of waste waters from the plant, in line with Levi's high enviroment protection standards, the radio said.

Vartex Denim, now employing 550 workers, has operated profitably since 1983 when it first signed a contract to produce Levi's jeans. Its prosperity has helped maintain other, less lucrative Vartex plants.
The company has a licence to produce all Levi's products except its exclusive '501' jeans. -- Laura Lui, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
